CBA2-R02.1.group_title: Waived compensation and current-season protection — Are earned, protected, unprotected, option, and bonus amounts separated on termination?
CBA2-R02.1.requirement: The dead-salary schedule ledger separately applies Contract protection and any approved buyout reduction; calculates set-off for each Salary Cap Year covered by the original Contract; when protected-Compensation payments are stretched under Article II §4(k), allocates that original Contract year's set-off equally across the applicable remaining payment stretch period; and, separately, when Team Salary is re-attributed under Article VII §7(d)(6), allocates that original Contract year's set-off equally to reduce the corresponding re-attributed Salary amounts across the applicable stretch period; no set-off arises for compensation earned after the original Contract term
CBA2-R02.1.basis: Dead salary is the guaranteed amount or full salary; there is no earned-vs-protected greater-of and no January 10 boundary.

CBA2-R02.2.group_title: Waived compensation and current-season protection — Are earned, protected, unprotected, option, and bonus amounts separated on termination?
CBA2-R02.2.requirement: Base Compensation for the current Season becomes protected for lack of skill on January 10 unless the Contract was terminated before that date; waiver timing is evaluated separately
CBA2-R02.2.basis: Dead salary is the guaranteed amount or full salary; there is no earned-vs-protected greater-of and no January 10 boundary.

CBA2-R02.4.group_title: Waived compensation and current-season protection — Are earned, protected, unprotected, option, and bonus amounts separated on termination?
CBA2-R02.4.requirement: Team Salary includes post-termination Salary attributable to a waived player after the approved buyout reduction is allocated under Article VII §7(d)(5) and any valid written Team Salary stretch election re-attributes Salary under §7(d)(6); set-off remains calculated by original Contract Salary Cap Year, and Article XXVII §5(b) allocates each affected original-year set-off equally to reduce the corresponding re-attributed Salary amounts across the applicable Team Salary stretch period
CBA2-R02.4.basis: Dead salary is the guaranteed amount or full salary; there is no earned-vs-protected greater-of and no January 10 boundary.

CBA2-R02.5.group_title: Waived compensation and current-season protection — Are earned, protected, unprotected, option, and bonus amounts separated on termination?
CBA2-R02.5.requirement: If a Contract terminates unclaimed, protected compensation remains as dead salary
CBA2-R02.5.basis: Dead salary is the guaranteed amount or full salary; there is no earned-vs-protected greater-of and no January 10 boundary.

CBA2-R02.6.group_title: Waived compensation and current-season protection — Are earned, protected, unprotected, option, and bonus amounts separated on termination?
CBA2-R02.6.requirement: Before January 10, current-year dead salary is the greater of earned base compensation and the protected amount
CBA2-R02.6.basis: Dead salary is the guaranteed amount or full salary; there is no earned-vs-protected greater-of and no January 10 boundary.

CBA2-R02.7.group_title: Waived compensation and current-season protection — Are earned, protected, unprotected, option, and bonus amounts separated on termination?
CBA2-R02.7.requirement: Dead-salary treatment follows the Contract’s exercised and protected compensation terms; an unexercised Team Option is not compensation protection, and Player Option treatment follows the signed option/protection language
CBA2-R02.7.basis: Dead salary is the guaranteed amount or full salary; there is no earned-vs-protected greater-of and no January 10 boundary.

CBA2-R02.8.group_title: Waived compensation and current-season protection — Are earned, protected, unprotected, option, and bonus amounts separated on termination?
CBA2-R02.8.requirement: On unclaimed termination, unearned unprotected Base Compensation and bonuses not earned before termination are excluded from the waived amount
CBA2-R02.8.basis: Dead salary is the guaranteed amount or full salary; there is no earned-vs-protected greater-of and no January 10 boundary.

CBA2-R02.9.group_title: Waived compensation and current-season protection — Are earned, protected, unprotected, option, and bonus amounts separated on termination?
CBA2-R02.9.requirement: The controlling waived amount supplied by CBA2-R02.6 is allocated to the affected Salary Cap Years under the Contract’s earned/protected compensation schedule
CBA2-R02.9.basis: Dead salary is the guaranteed amount or full salary; there is no earned-vs-protected greater-of and no January 10 boundary.

CBA2-R03.1.group_title: Waived veteran-minimum compensation basis — Does dead salary use actual Base Compensation rather than a reimbursement-adjusted Team Salary amount?
CBA2-R03.1.requirement: A waived veteran-minimum player’s actual Base Compensation, not a reimbursement-adjusted Team Salary amount, controls the player-compensation obligation and resulting waived amount
CBA2-R03.1.basis: waiverDeadCapAllocation reads row.salary rather than the subsidised capHit, which satisfies the rule by construction, but nothing states or tests the rule.

CBA2-R03.2.group_title: Waived veteran-minimum compensation basis — Does dead salary use actual Base Compensation rather than a reimbursement-adjusted Team Salary amount?
CBA2-R03.2.requirement: League reimbursement and Team Salary treatment for a qualifying veteran-minimum Contract remain separate from the player’s Base Compensation and the waiving Team’s payment obligation
CBA2-R03.2.basis: waiverDeadCapAllocation reads row.salary rather than the subsidised capHit, which satisfies the rule by construction, but nothing states or tests the rule.

CBA2-R04.1.group_title: Payment stretching and Team Salary stretching — Are payment timing and Team Salary allocation treated as separate elections with exact timing and limits?
CBA2-R04.1.requirement: A valid Team Salary stretch election allocates applicable waived salary over twice the remaining contract Seasons plus one
CBA2-R04.1.basis: The (2n+1) stretch term is correct; the September 1 election branch is only a soft warning and the 15%-of-cap limit is absent (zero hits).

CBA2-R04.2.group_title: Payment stretching and Team Salary stretching — Are payment timing and Team Salary allocation treated as separate elections with exact timing and limits?
CBA2-R04.2.requirement: A July 1 through August 31 Team Salary stretch includes the current Salary Cap Year in the 2n+1 period; a September 1 through June 30 election leaves the current year unchanged and stretches only future amounts
CBA2-R04.2.basis: The (2n+1) stretch term is correct; the September 1 election branch is only a soft warning and the 15%-of-cap limit is absent (zero hits).

CBA2-R04.3.group_title: Payment stretching and Team Salary stretching — Are payment timing and Team Salary allocation treated as separate elections with exact timing and limits?
CBA2-R04.3.requirement: The contract must be terminated before the September 1 preceding its final season, and the stretch elected before that same September 1
CBA2-R04.3.basis: The (2n+1) stretch term is correct; the September 1 election branch is only a soft warning and the 15%-of-cap limit is absent (zero hits).

CBA2-R04.4.group_title: Payment stretching and Team Salary stretching — Are payment timing and Team Salary allocation treated as separate elections with exact timing and limits?
CBA2-R04.4.requirement: A stretch is unavailable if future-year Team Salary attributable to all waived/former players already exceeds, or would exceed, 15% of the cap in effect at election
CBA2-R04.4.basis: The (2n+1) stretch term is correct; the September 1 election branch is only a soft warning and the 15%-of-cap limit is absent (zero hits).

CBA2-R04.5.group_title: Payment stretching and Team Salary stretching — Are payment timing and Team Salary allocation treated as separate elections with exact timing and limits?
CBA2-R04.5.requirement: A team that stretches cannot re-sign or reacquire the player before the July 1 following the last season of the terminated contract, including an option year
CBA2-R04.5.basis: The (2n+1) stretch term is correct; the September 1 election branch is only a soft warning and the 15%-of-cap limit is absent (zero hits).

CBA2-R04.7.group_title: Payment stretching and Team Salary stretching — Are payment timing and Team Salary allocation treated as separate elections with exact timing and limits?
CBA2-R04.7.requirement: A payment-stretch election uses the mandatory payment schedule in Article II §4(k) and does not alter Team Salary unless the Team separately makes a valid Article VII §7(d)(6) election
CBA2-R04.7.basis: The (2n+1) stretch term is correct; the September 1 election branch is only a soft warning and the 15%-of-cap limit is absent (zero hits).

CBA2-R04.9.group_title: Payment stretching and Team Salary stretching — Are payment timing and Team Salary allocation treated as separate elections with exact timing and limits?
CBA2-R04.9.requirement: Total Salaries and player-payment obligations are unaffected by the Article VII Team Salary stretch allocation
CBA2-R04.9.basis: The (2n+1) stretch term is correct; the September 1 election branch is only a soft warning and the 15%-of-cap limit is absent (zero hits).

CBA2-R05.1.group_title: Buyout, set-off, and reacquisition lifecycle — Are reduced protection, set-off, allocation, waivers, and later signing restrictions applied separately?
CBA2-R05.1.requirement: A buyout is a written agreement that reduces protected compensation in exchange for release
CBA2-R05.1.basis: Buyout produces reduced dead cap; proportional reduction and later set-off reconciliation are not modelled.

CBA2-R05.2.group_title: Buyout, set-off, and reacquisition lifecycle — Are reduced protection, set-off, allocation, waivers, and later signing restrictions applied separately?
CBA2-R05.2.requirement: Set-off can reduce a prior team's obligation when the waived player earns compensation elsewhere during the original term
CBA2-R05.2.basis: Buyout produces reduced dead cap; proportional reduction and later set-off reconciliation are not modelled.

CBA2-R05.3.group_title: Buyout, set-off, and reacquisition lifecycle — Are reduced protection, set-off, allocation, waivers, and later signing restrictions applied separately?
CBA2-R05.3.requirement: Set-off routing selects the NBA, non-NBA, or successive/deferred compensation branch and reports the direct branch result without recomputing it
CBA2-R05.3.basis: Buyout produces reduced dead cap; proportional reduction and later set-off reconciliation are not modelled.

CBA2-R05.4.group_title: Buyout, set-off, and reacquisition lifecycle — Are reduced protection, set-off, allocation, waivers, and later signing restrictions applied separately?
CBA2-R05.4.requirement: Set-off reductions follow the applicable waived-salary allocation; set-off may be waived or modified only through the written Article II §3(p) contract term
CBA2-R05.4.basis: Buyout produces reduced dead cap; proportional reduction and later set-off reconciliation are not modelled.

CBA2-R05.5.group_title: Buyout, set-off, and reacquisition lifecycle — Are reduced protection, set-off, allocation, waivers, and later signing restrictions applied separately?
CBA2-R05.5.requirement: After a buyout or trade-and-waive, the applicable prior-Team signing or reacquisition bar lasts through the later of one year after the transaction and July 1 following the last Season of the terminated Contract
CBA2-R05.5.basis: Buyout produces reduced dead cap; proportional reduction and later set-off reconciliation are not modelled.

CBA2-R05.6.group_title: Buyout, set-off, and reacquisition lifecycle — Are reduced protection, set-off, allocation, waivers, and later signing restrictions applied separately?
CBA2-R05.6.requirement: A buyout allocates the reduced protected Base Compensation pro rata over the current and remaining Seasons according to remaining unearned protected Base Compensation
CBA2-R05.6.basis: Buyout produces reduced dead cap; proportional reduction and later set-off reconciliation are not modelled.

CBA2-R05.7.group_title: Buyout, set-off, and reacquisition lifecycle — Are reduced protection, set-off, allocation, waivers, and later signing restrictions applied separately?
CBA2-R05.7.requirement: NBA set-off equals fifty percent of the positive excess of new Base Compensation over the applicable zero- or one-YOS Minimum Player Salary
CBA2-R05.7.basis: Buyout produces reduced dead cap; proportional reduction and later set-off reconciliation are not modelled.

CBA2-R05.8.group_title: Buyout, set-off, and reacquisition lifecycle — Are reduced protection, set-off, allocation, waivers, and later signing restrictions applied separately?
CBA2-R05.8.requirement: Non-NBA set-off is optional and, when exercised, applies the signed net-of-tax and 0.65 treatment rather than the NBA formula unchanged
CBA2-R05.8.basis: Buyout produces reduced dead cap; proportional reduction and later set-off reconciliation are not modelled.

CBA2-R05.9.group_title: Buyout, set-off, and reacquisition lifecycle — Are reduced protection, set-off, allocation, waivers, and later signing restrictions applied separately?
CBA2-R05.9.requirement: Successive terminations apply set-off in the signed order, and deferred compensation is discounted as Article XXVII requires
CBA2-R05.9.basis: Buyout produces reduced dead cap; proportional reduction and later set-off reconciliation are not modelled.

CBA2-R05.10.group_title: Buyout, set-off, and reacquisition lifecycle — Are reduced protection, set-off, allocation, waivers, and later signing restrictions applied separately?
CBA2-R05.10.requirement: No payment or Team Salary allocation extends beyond the original Contract term except a valid elected stretch allocation under its own rule
CBA2-R05.10.basis: Buyout produces reduced dead cap; proportional reduction and later set-off reconciliation are not modelled.

CBA2-R06.1.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.1.requirement: Roster state separately records Standard Contracts, Active List players, Inactive List players, Two-Way Contracts, bench availability, and offseason aggregate count
CBA2-R06.1.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.2.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.2.requirement: Combined-list compliance is a staged result that reports whether the direct fourteen-to-fifteen bound, including the direct Two-Way increment, passes for the as-of-date list snapshot
CBA2-R06.2.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.3.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.3.requirement: Temporary combined-list compliance is a staged result that reports the current end-of-day shortage count, consecutive interval, Season total, and the direct twelve-or-thirteen allowance result
CBA2-R06.3.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.4.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.4.requirement: Active-List compliance is a staged result that reports the direct ordinary bound and, when the count is eleven, the separate consecutive and Season-total allowance result
CBA2-R06.4.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.5.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.5.requirement: Game-bench compliance is the staged game-level result of applying the direct eight-player availability rule to the authenticated Active List and availability snapshot
CBA2-R06.5.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.6.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.6.requirement: Two-Way roster compliance is a staged result that reports the direct Contract maximum, the total-player Active List bound, and the separate combined-list Two-Way increment for the as-of-date list snapshot
CBA2-R06.6.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.7.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.7.requirement: The ordinary Active List minimum is twelve and maximum is fifteen total players, including any Two-Way Player placed on the Active List
CBA2-R06.7.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.8.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.8.requirement: The ordinary combined Active and Inactive List minimum is fourteen and maximum is fifteen, with each Two-Way player on either list increasing both bounds by one
CBA2-R06.8.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.9.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.9.requirement: A day counts toward the temporary combined-list limits when the Team has fewer than fourteen players in aggregate on its Active and Inactive Lists at the end of that day
CBA2-R06.9.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.10.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.10.requirement: A temporary combined-list allowance permits twelve or thirteen players during the Regular Season for no more than two consecutive weeks and no more than twenty-eight total days in the Season
CBA2-R06.10.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.11.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.11.requirement: The temporary Active List allowance permits eleven players for no more than two consecutive weeks and no more than twenty-eight total days in a Season
CBA2-R06.11.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.12.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.12.requirement: At least eight players on the Active List must be available on the bench for a game unless a controlling exception applies
CBA2-R06.12.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.13.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.13.requirement: The offseason aggregate maximum is twenty-one across Standard and Two-Way players after the league-wide Season transition
CBA2-R06.13.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.14.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.14.requirement: The ordinary maximum number of Two-Way Contracts is three before any valid Article XXIX §5 adjustment
CBA2-R06.14.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.15.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.15.requirement: Two consecutive qualifying league-wide averages below 14.25 permanently raise the Standard-contract minimum to fifteen and adjust the temporary shortage bands
CBA2-R06.15.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R06.16.group_title: Standard, Active, Inactive, bench, and Two-Way counts — Are every ordinary and temporary roster/list bound and Two-Way increment enforced independently?
CBA2-R06.16.requirement: Two consecutive qualifying league-wide averages below 14.5 give the Players Association a forty-five-day option to reduce the Two-Way maximum to two
CBA2-R06.16.basis: 15-standard/3-two-way bounds are hard blocks and 14 is a soft warning; Active/Inactive/bench lists and the temporary 12/13 states do not exist.

CBA2-R07.1.group_title: Short-roster clocks — Are the consecutive-week and season-total shortage clocks measured and persisted from the correct day state?
CBA2-R07.1.requirement: For each shortage band, state persists both the consecutive-shortage interval and the independent total count of qualifying end-of-day shortage days in the Season
CBA2-R07.1.basis: Only a comment records the 13-for-14-days allowance; no consecutive or season-total clock is measured or persisted.

CBA2-R07.2.group_title: Short-roster clocks — Are the consecutive-week and season-total shortage clocks measured and persisted from the correct day state?
CBA2-R07.2.requirement: The two-consecutive-week clock and twenty-eight-total-day clock are independent; leaving the shortage band resets only the consecutive clock
CBA2-R07.2.basis: Only a comment records the 13-for-14-days allowance; no consecutive or season-total clock is measured or persisted.

CBA2-R07.3.group_title: Short-roster clocks — Are the consecutive-week and season-total shortage clocks measured and persisted from the correct day state?
CBA2-R07.3.requirement: Each shortage clock is keyed to its governing Active-only or combined-list band so one band cannot satisfy or consume the other band’s allowance
CBA2-R07.3.basis: Only a comment records the 13-for-14-days allowance; no consecutive or season-total clock is measured or persisted.

CBA2-R08.1.group_title: Two-Way active-game and Under-Fifteen-Games accounting — Are player and team usage limits computed separately with their signing-time and roster-count conditions?
CBA2-R08.1.basis: No two-way active-game or Under-Fifteen-Games accounting exists.

CBA2-R08.2.group_title: Two-Way active-game and Under-Fifteen-Games accounting — Are player and team usage limits computed separately with their signing-time and roster-count conditions?
CBA2-R08.2.basis: No two-way active-game or Under-Fifteen-Games accounting exists.

CBA2-R08.3.group_title: Two-Way active-game and Under-Fifteen-Games accounting — Are player and team usage limits computed separately with their signing-time and roster-count conditions?
CBA2-R08.3.requirement: A Two-Way player signed for the full Season may be active for no more than fifty games
CBA2-R08.3.basis: No two-way active-game or Under-Fifteen-Games accounting exists.

CBA2-R08.4.group_title: Two-Way active-game and Under-Fifteen-Games accounting — Are player and team usage limits computed separately with their signing-time and roster-count conditions?
CBA2-R08.4.requirement: A Team may not exceed ninety Under-Fifteen Games in the Season
CBA2-R08.4.basis: No two-way active-game or Under-Fifteen-Games accounting exists.

CBA2-R08.5.group_title: Two-Way active-game and Under-Fifteen-Games accounting — Are player and team usage limits computed separately with their signing-time and roster-count conditions?
CBA2-R08.5.requirement: The usage-ledger snapshot reports each Two-Way player’s applicable active-game maximum and count plus the Team’s Under-Fifteen maximum and count at the requested as-of date
CBA2-R08.5.basis: No two-way active-game or Under-Fifteen-Games accounting exists.

CBA2-R08.6.group_title: Two-Way active-game and Under-Fifteen-Games accounting — Are player and team usage limits computed separately with their signing-time and roster-count conditions?
CBA2-R08.6.requirement: The fifty-game Two-Way Active List maximum is prorated under the signed late-signing rule rather than assumed to remain fifty
CBA2-R08.6.basis: No two-way active-game or Under-Fifteen-Games accounting exists.

CBA2-R08.7.group_title: Two-Way active-game and Under-Fifteen-Games accounting — Are player and team usage limits computed separately with their signing-time and roster-count conditions?
CBA2-R08.7.requirement: An Under-Fifteen Game accrues only when a Two-Way player is active while the Team has fewer than fifteen Standard Contracts under the signed counting rule
CBA2-R08.7.basis: No two-way active-game or Under-Fifteen-Games accounting exists.

CBA2-R09.2.group_title: Offseason roster transition and capacity — Does the league-wide end-of-Season event move list status and activate the aggregate offseason maximum?
CBA2-R09.2.requirement: On the day after the last day of the league Season, Inactive and Two-Way players transfer to the offseason Active List; one playoff Team’s elimination does not start that transition
CBA2-R09.2.basis: Season advance moves 30 teams and rolls contracts; the offseason 21-man capacity and merged list categories are absent.

CBA2-R09.3.group_title: Offseason roster transition and capacity — Does the league-wide end-of-Season event move list status and activate the aggregate offseason maximum?
CBA2-R09.3.requirement: The CBA2-R06.13 offseason aggregate applies from the league-wide Season transition through the day before the next Regular Season
CBA2-R09.3.basis: Season advance moves 30 teams and rolls contracts; the offseason 21-man capacity and merged list categories are absent.

CBA2-R10.1.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.1.requirement: Each player’s contract type and current Active, Inactive, Two-Way, Voluntarily Retired, Suspended, or other governed list state are persisted independently
CBA2-R10.1.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.2.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.2.requirement: Hardship and treatment-program capacity require the exact approval, medical/treatment, missed-game, and effective-period inputs stated by the controlling rule
CBA2-R10.2.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.3.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.3.requirement: Suspended-list route status reports whether the League-suspension or Team-suspension direct branch is eligible and identifies the first unmet branch condition
CBA2-R10.3.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.4.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.4.requirement: Excess-capacity route status reports whether the special fourth-injury hardship or treatment-program direct branch is available and identifies any required external approval
CBA2-R10.4.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.5.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.5.requirement: A League-suspended player becomes eligible for the governed Suspended List move only after serving the fifth suspension game
CBA2-R10.5.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.6.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.6.requirement: A Team-suspended player becomes eligible for the governed Suspended List move only after serving the third suspension game and the Team gives the required written notice
CBA2-R10.6.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.7.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.7.requirement: The special fourth-injury hardship route requires four players who each missed three consecutive games plus an express Commissioner determination
CBA2-R10.7.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.8.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.8.requirement: A treatment-program player may permit roster capacity above fifteen only after inpatient treatment and three consecutive missed games under the signed program rule
CBA2-R10.8.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.9.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.9.requirement: Hardship approval records identify the player, Team, factual basis, approving authority, effective date, scope, and expiration or superseding event
CBA2-R10.9.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.10.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.10.requirement: A medical or treatment determination changes roster state only for its authenticated scope and effective period and never from a guessed diagnosis
CBA2-R10.10.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.11.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.11.requirement: Two-Way and NBA G League suspension/list consequences use their controlling CBA and league rules rather than the ordinary Standard-player suspension threshold by analogy
CBA2-R10.11.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-R10.12.group_title: Suspension, hardship, treatment, and externally determined roster states — Are list changes tied to exact served-game, medical, approval, and treatment inputs instead of inferred outcomes?
CBA2-R10.12.requirement: Voluntarily Retired, Suspended, and treatment-program states remain distinct from Active, Inactive, and Two-Way list capacity and retain their triggering record
CBA2-R10.12.basis: No hardship, suspension-list or treatment-program state.

CBA2-L01.1.group_title: Explicit transaction date and season calendar — Is each result keyed to an explicit as-of date, Salary Cap Year, and authoritative season calendar?
CBA2-L01.1.requirement: Every determination is evaluated for an explicit as-of date and Salary Cap Year; a runtime default such as today may not substitute for those inputs

CBA2-L07.3.group_title: Hard-cap state — Does each hard cap retain its level, trigger transaction, start, and governing Salary Cap Year end?

CBA2-L07.3.basis: hardCapLevel/Type/Trigger/Year/Reason are stored and persisted; explicit start and governing-year-end instants are not, and only first-apron caps can arise.

CBA2-L08.3.basis: No multi-season taxpayer or Second Apron history is retained, so repeater status and frozen-pick penalties cannot be derived.

CBA2-L08.4.group_title: Taxpayer, Second Apron, frozen-pick, and penalty history — Is multi-season tax and apron history measured at the signed observation point and retained through every pick-state transition?

CBA2-L08.4.basis: No multi-season taxpayer or Second Apron history is retained, so repeater status and frozen-pick penalties cannot be derived.

CBA2-L08.5.group_title: Taxpayer, Second Apron, frozen-pick, and penalty history — Is multi-season tax and apron history measured at the signed observation point and retained through every pick-state transition?
CBA2-L08.5.requirement: Persistent team-apron observations and pick-status transitions, rather than current-year validation alone, control frozen-pick and penalty outcomes
CBA2-L08.5.basis: No multi-season taxpayer or Second Apron history is retained, so repeater status and frozen-pick penalties cannot be derived.

CBA2-L08.7.group_title: Taxpayer, Second Apron, frozen-pick, and penalty history — Is multi-season tax and apron history measured at the signed observation point and retained through every pick-state transition?
CBA2-L08.7.requirement: A Team above the Second Apron in at least two of the four measurement Seasons receives the Draft Pick Penalty on its final first-round pick
CBA2-L08.7.basis: No multi-season taxpayer or Second Apron history is retained, so repeater status and frozen-pick penalties cannot be derived.

CBA2-L08.8.group_title: Taxpayer, Second Apron, frozen-pick, and penalty history — Is multi-season tax and apron history measured at the signed observation point and retained through every pick-state transition?
CBA2-L08.8.requirement: When multiple first-round picks carry the Draft Pick Penalty, their end-of-round order is inverse winning percentage under the signed rule

CBA2-L09.1.requirement: For a pick governed by Article VII §2(f), the ledger aggregates the accepted freeze/unfreeze/no-penalty results and the direct penalty/placement results without re-deciding any component

CBA2-L09.3.group_title: Pick ledger and conveyance state — Do ownership, availability, conditions, deferrals, freezes, penalties, and unfreezes coexist in one date-aware pick ledger?
CBA2-L09.3.requirement: A dated first-round-pick availability result may enforce only the direct Article VII §2(f) frozen-pick state and the By-Laws §7.03 consecutive-future-Drafts prohibition; any unresolved protection or deferral branch is reported unavailable, not guessed
CBA2-L09.3.basis: A large date-aware pick/conveyance/protection surface exists; freezes, penalties and unfreezes are not part of it.

CBA2-L09.4.group_title: Pick ledger and conveyance state — Do ownership, availability, conditions, deferrals, freezes, penalties, and unfreezes coexist in one date-aware pick ledger?
CBA2-L09.4.requirement: The governed pick-status record preserves owned, frozen, unfrozen, penalized, and exact “slid status” placement states as separate fields sourced from their direct results
CBA2-L09.4.basis: A large date-aware pick/conveyance/protection surface exists; freezes, penalties and unfreezes are not part of it.

CBA2-L09.6.group_title: Pick ledger and conveyance state — Do ownership, availability, conditions, deferrals, freezes, penalties, and unfreezes coexist in one date-aware pick ledger?
CBA2-L09.6.requirement: A Member may not trade or exchange a first-round selection right when the result may leave it without first-round picks in any two consecutive future NBA Drafts
CBA2-L09.6.basis: A large date-aware pick/conveyance/protection surface exists; freezes, penalties and unfreezes are not part of it.

CBA2-L10.6.group_title: Authenticated external determinations — Can medical, expert, grievance, approval, and conduct determinations be supplied explicitly with provenance and bounded effect?

CBA2-L10.7.group_title: Authenticated external determinations — Can medical, expert, grievance, approval, and conduct determinations be supplied explicitly with provenance and bounded effect?
CBA2-L10.7.requirement: Disputed amounts and authenticated grievance awards or settlements may be entered and allocated; the award itself is never predicted

CBA2-L10.9.group_title: Authenticated external determinations — Can medical, expert, grievance, approval, and conduct determinations be supplied explicitly with provenance and bounded effect?
CBA2-L10.9.requirement: Every unresolved EXT state is reported as external determination or assumption required and never as an unqualified pass or fail
CBA2-L10.9.basis: capRulesProfile carries source provenance for cap values, but there is no way to set a medical, expert, grievance or league determination explicitly.

CBA2-L10.10.group_title: Authenticated external determinations — Can medical, expert, grievance, approval, and conduct determinations be supplied explicitly with provenance and bounded effect?
CBA2-L10.10.requirement: Each authenticated external determination retains a supersession chain so a later ruling changes only its stated scope and does not erase the prior decision history

CBA2-S04.1.group_title: Derived and indexed amounts — Are formulas evaluated from published inputs with only rule-defined rounding and no false fixed constants?
CBA2-S04.1.requirement: Expanded-TPE formula-provenance status confirms that the historical A/crossover fragment is represented by accepted CBA2-A02.8 and that its season-keyed input record IDs are retained
CBA2-S04.1.basis: capRulesProfile derives the rookie minimum from published cap growth with recorded provenance — a correct derived-amount route — while salaryMatchingRules and validateCash keep false fixed constants.

CBA2-S04.2.group_title: Derived and indexed amounts — Are formulas evaluated from published inputs with only rule-defined rounding and no false fixed constants?
CBA2-S04.2.requirement: Indexed-value readiness is a staged result that reports whether the BAE, cash-limit, EIPPA, and Tax Bracket Amount direct owners each resolved for the same requested Salary Cap Year and identifies any missing or mismatched component
CBA2-S04.2.basis: Rookie-minimum projection is genuinely derived from published cap growth; the Expanded TPE and cash limits are false fixed constants that should be formula-evaluated.

CBA2-S04.3.basis: Rookie-minimum projection is genuinely derived from published cap growth; the Expanded TPE and cash limits are false fixed constants that should be formula-evaluated.
